title: Move Semantics
story: When your friend borrows your favorite book and you never see it again — that's a move, not a borrow. In XIOM, assignment is a move by default.
why: Move semantics are the default in XIOM because they are zero-cost — no copying, no reference counting, just a simple pointer swap.
analogy: Assignment is like handing someone your wallet — you no longer have it, they do. If you try to spend from a wallet you already gave away, that's fraud.
try_it: Try adding `io.println(v.len());` after the move to `moved_v`. See the compiler error about using a moved value.
tips: Assignment (=) is always a move in XIOM, never a copy
A move is cheap — it only copies the pointer, not the data
The compiler tracks every variable's ownership status at compile time
If you need a copy, use .clone() explicitly
common_mistakes: Assuming = copies values — it doesn't, it moves them
Trying to use a variable after passing it to a function — functions take ownership too
Forgetting that returning a value from a function also moves it
